# Kanon — [Worship / liturgy / chant — Eastern Orthodox]
**Claim:** A subscription SaaS for Orthodox chanters and parish priests that auto-generates the complete assembled service text for any day — resolving Typikon coincidences (feast-day conflicts across the fixed Menaion, Octoechos, Triodion, Pentecostarion cycles) — and outputs a formatted, print-ready chanter's run-sheet in the parish's preferred language, a task that currently requires an expert typikaris spending 2-4 hours per service.
**Why-now capability:** LLMs capable of following complex conditional rule systems (the Typikon precedence table has ~300 ranked feast categories with interaction rules) and generating structured multi-section documents became reliable in 2024-2025, with long-context models able to hold all four liturgical books' relevant sections in context simultaneously. This is not free-form generation — it is deterministic rule-following with LLM-assisted disambiguation for edge cases.
**Mechanism / rationale:** Captive-distribution plus self-handicapped-incumbent: Canticle serves Episcopal, Precentor serves Church of England, OCP Liturgy.com serves Roman Catholic, Church Music & Liturgy Planner and Asaph.io serve Protestant — none cover Eastern Orthodox. The Greek Archdiocese's Digital Chant Stand distributes static PDFs prepared annually by Fr. Seraphim Dedes — not generative, not interactive, only the Greek Archdiocese's Typikon interpretation. No shipped SaaS auto-resolves Byzantine Typikon conflicts; the only scholarly attempt was an unpublished master's thesis. Payer: parish priest or chanters' committee ($19-39/month per parish); distribution via Orthodox seminaries (Holy Cross, St. Vladimir's, St. Tikhon's) and the ~5,000 active North American parishes. Proprietary corpus deepens as each jurisdiction's customizations (calendar variant, local saints, translation preferences) are stored per-parish.
**Novelty:** No shipped product auto-assembles Eastern Orthodox service books by resolving Typikon coincidences. The only verified tool (Digital Chant Stand) is a static annual PDF repository. The Typikon rule system is complex enough that incumbents from adjacent traditions cannot copy it without rebuilding the domain logic from scratch.
**Test:** Partner with 5 Orthodox parishes (Greek, Antiochian, OCA) for a 90-day pilot. Kanon generates assembled weekday and Sunday service texts for 12 weeks. Measure: (a) chanter-rated accuracy of Typikon conflict resolution vs. the parish typikaris, (b) time savings per service, (c) does the PDF land on the chanter's stand. Success: >85% accuracy by an independent typikaris reviewer, >1 hour saved per service, 4 of 5 parishes request continued access.
**Assumptions:** (1) The Typikon, while complex, is fully codified — a deterministic algorithm with LLM assistance only for ambiguous edge cases. (2) Liturgical texts required are public domain (pre-1923 Greek/Slavonic; English translations from public-domain or open-licensed sources). (3) At least one team member is a practicing Orthodox Christian with chanting experience to validate outputs. Doctrinal-accuracy gate: all generated texts are sourced to specific liturgical books with citations; the product never invents liturgical text — it assembles from the corpus. No pastoral/crisis function.
